question: Under whose leadership did the Khalsa revolt against the Mughal rule after the death of Guru Gobind Singh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Banda Bahadur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Banda Bahadur**, also known as Lachman Das, was a notable Sikh military commander and leader. After the death of **Guru Gobind Singh** in 1708, Banda Bahadur led the **Khalsa** in a revolt against the oppressive **Mughal rule** in northern India.
 
• Banda Bahadur was appointed by Guru Gobind Singh to lead the Sikh army and take the struggle for justice forward. He became the first Sikh military leader to establish **Sikh sovereignty** in Punjab.
 
• Under his leadership, the Sikh army achieved significant victories against the Mughals, notably the capture of **Samana** in 1709, where he redistributed land to peasants, aligning with Sikh values of social justice and equality.
 
• He issued the **first Sikh coins** in the name of Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh, symbolizing the establishment of Sikh political authority.
 
• Banda Bahadur is remembered for his efforts to uplift the oppressed and his ability to unite the Sikh community against the tyranny of the Mughal Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Guru Gobind Singh:**

 
 
• He was the tenth Sikh Guru, who founded the **Khalsa** in 1699 to fight against oppression and uphold justice and righteousness.
 
• Before his death in 1708, Guru Gobind Singh passed the leadership of the Sikh community to the **Guru Granth Sahib** (the Sikh holy scripture) and appointed Banda Bahadur to lead the military struggle.
 
 
 
• **Banda Bahadur’s Campaigns:**
 
 
• One of his most significant victories was the battle of **Sirhind** in 1710, where the Mughal governor Wazir Khan was defeated.
 
• Banda Bahadur's policies focused on redistributing land to the poor and removing feudal oppression, which made him popular among peasants and the lower classes.
 
 
 
• **Downfall and Legacy:**
 
 
• Banda Bahadur was eventually captured by the Mughal forces in 1715 and executed in 1716 in Delhi after being tortured for months.
 
• Despite his tragic end, Banda Bahadur’s legacy lives on as a symbol of courage, sacrifice, and the fight against tyranny.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Chattar Singh Attriwal:** He was a Sikh leader during the **Sikh Empire**, but he did not lead the Khalsa revolt post Guru Gobind Singh's death.
 
• **Duleep Singh:** He was the last Maharaja of the Sikh Empire and not related to the Khalsa revolt after Guru Gobind Singh's death.
 
• **Udai Singh:** A Rajput king and not associated with Sikh history or the Khalsa revolt.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Banda Bahadur’s Policies:**

 
 
• He abolished the **zamindari system** and granted land to the tillers, which was revolutionary for the time.
 
• He introduced Sikh principles of equality and justice in the governance of captured territories.
 
 
 
• **Khalsa Army:**
 
 
• The Khalsa was a military and spiritual order established by **Guru Gobind Singh**.
 
• Under Banda Bahadur, the Khalsa transformed into a formidable force challenging the Mughal Empire.
